cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what you are is already on the page.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you do well and describe it plainly to one person this week — no downplaying, no running it down first.
cells.core: You're working from what you actually are rather than a version of it, and it holds up fine without an audience. The glow comes off a person at ease in their own shape — they don't announce it, they just take up the room they take up. When a split or a load needs adjusting between people, you do it from the middle, not from a side, and it comes out even without anyone arguing for it. People leave that exchange lighter and rarely stop to ask why.\n\nThe tell is that nothing is being proved. Notice where you nearly start explaining and let the work answer instead. What you are isn't the argument you make for it. It's the thing already showing, doing its quiet work whether or not anyone names it.
cells.sheetLine: You shine because you are it, not to prove it.
cells.place: Where things get weighed and set right between people

cells.tense: You are pressing tomorrow's version of yourself into rooms that haven't opened yet.
cells.ask: Find one place where you're over-explaining what you're becoming and say less than feels finished.
cells.core: Somewhere ahead sits a fully formed version of this, undeniable, and you lean toward that picture while the rooms you're actually in get what's left over. Your real glow gets used as a spotlight on a moment that hasn't come, and it lands on people as glare instead of warmth. The forward lean isn't a flaw in the light — it's the extra weight riding on top of it.\n\nWatch what the lean does to your attention: the room in front of you goes blurry and you can't feel whether anyone is with you. Set the future down for one exchange and stand where you actually are. The balance sits closer than the picture does.
cells.sheetLine: You're proving the shine instead of being in it.

cells.tense: You are already what you are, and you are still standing at a door behind you.
cells.ask: Say one finished thing you made, even small, without adding a qualifier to soften it.
cells.core: This has been showing up in you for a while, and you keep describing it as almost. You shrink what you've already reached, and the shrinking reads to others as modesty, so nobody corrects it — the honest size of it sits there unclaimed. You can watch the move happen: the thing is done, and then a quiet sentence arrives to take the edge off it.\n\nThe moment just before that softening is the one to catch. Say the true size of one thing out loud once, and let it stand there with no cushion under it. Nothing about what you've become needs to be earned back first.
cells.sheetLine: You've already become it. You keep calling it almost.
cells.place: Where things get weighed and set right between people

cells.tense: You are already showing what you are, and you keep filing it under something else.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did today that made a situation fairer, and count it as yours.
cells.core: The showing carries on now — in how you hold a room, adjust a sentence, wait for someone slower to reach the same place. What you are lives in those small moves, and they're already doing work. You just file them under the situation, or the other person, or the day. Meanwhile it's your hand on the scale.\n\nMiss it long enough and the shine gets credited to the room instead of the one who lit it. Stay with the next thing that arrives and let it be fresh instead of a rerun. The turning isn't waiting for you later. You're the turning now.
cells.sheetLine: You're already doing it. Start claiming it as yours.

The reader could say 'I'm not doing any of this' — and that is fine, because the ask is a low-cost act that still teaches something even if the read is wrong. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any poetic line about 'your light' that flatters rather than points, so I'm keeping the images plain and earned. The ask survives being wrong: it is a single tuning act, not a diagnosis.
